pages.text: $(bold)Protection$(0)$(br)A short circuit draws enormous current.$(br2)$(li)$(thing)Fuses$(0) melt when overloaded. Adjust their rating while holding Ctrl and scrolling, and replace them when they blow.$(li)$(thing)Miniature Circuit Breakers$(0) trip and can be reset.$(li)$(thing)SF6 Breakers$(0) switch high-voltage lines, their arc smothered in sulfur hexafluoride.

$(bold)Measuring$(0)$(br)$(li)$(thing)Ammeter$(0): placed in series, along the wire, reads the current$(li)$(thing)Voltmeter$(0): placed in parallel, across two wires, reads the voltage$(li)$(thing)Energy Meters$(0) total the energy delivered$(li)The $(thing)Clamp Meter$(0) reads the current in any wire you point it at

$(bold)Switching and control$(0)$(br)Cut-off switches, relays, potentiometers and variacs control the circuit. Redstone versions let contraptions do the switching.$(br2)The $(thing)Voltage Regulator$(0) holds its output steady while the load changes.
Nickel-iron $(thing)Accumulators$(0) store energy at 24 V. Wire them in series for higher voltages: ten in a row charge at 240 V.
The $(thing)Resistive Heater$(0) turns current into heat. It heats boilers, basins and TFMG vats placed above it, just like a burner.

$(bold)Light$(0)$(br)$(thing)Bulbs$(0) are tungsten-filament lamps in brass sockets. They stop mobs spawning even when switched off. A burnt-out bulb is repaired with a new tungsten wire.$(br2)$(thing)Indicator Bulbs$(0) are small signal lights you can dye.
